text: Thus, although the research on the topic remains equivocal and is confounded by the aforementioned limitations, the literature does seem to suggest a potential benefit for systematically manipulating variables over time to maximize hypertrophic adaptations, and the logical basis of the approach advocates employing periodization for the goal of muscle building. Moreover, considerable evidence shows that periodization elicits greater gains in strength than nonperiodized approaches do (1, 94, 96, 132, 147). Given that mechanical tension is a primary driving force for muscle protein accretion (116), a case can be made that greater increases in strength alone would facilitate superior hypertrophic gains over time. provides a summary of the research related to periodized versus nonperiodized
